projects.title: Aceitar Moscato — Wine Label
projects.summary: A dark, gold-detailed wine label with braille text, shown flat, rendered in 3D and mocked up in a styled shoot.
projects.description: Label and brand identity for Aceitar Moscato. The dark bottle, gold line illustration and tactile braille detail are designed to read as premium on a shelf and to carry across the whole bottle, front and back.
projects.brief: Create a label that feels premium and distinctive for a Moscato, and check how it wraps around a real bottle before print.
process: Designed the label artwork flat, front and back.
Built 3D renders of the bottle to check legibility, scale and how the label wraps.
Placed the final design in a lifestyle mockup with a glass of wine.

projects.title: One Pass — Office Branding
projects.summary: A brand-colored interior: dimensional wall logo, painted wall graphic and a patterned glass covering, all drawn for production.
projects.description: Interior branding for the One Pass office. The logo and its looping mark were adapted to three different surfaces — wall, paint and glass — and documented in dimensioned shop drawings so each could be produced and installed accurately.
projects.brief: Carry the One Pass brand through an open-plan office using a wall logo, a large painted graphic and a frosted pattern on the conference-room glass.
process: Rendered the graphics onto photos of the space for approval.
Drew shop drawings with dimensions, materials, ink layers and notes for production.
Documented the painted wall in progress and the installed result.

projects.title: TidyPaws — Packaging
projects.summary: Kraft tube packaging with a hand-drawn animal for each scent.
projects.description: Packaging design for TidyPaws: a natural kraft tube with one illustrated animal character per variety. The system flexes by color and character while the type and layout stay consistent.
projects.brief: Design a packaging family that looks natural and friendly and is easy to tell apart by scent at a glance.
process: Illustrated a character for each variety.
Built a label system where color and illustration change and everything else stays fixed.
Mocked up the tubes in a realistic setting to check the look in context.

projects.title: Minneapolis Pickleball Club — Exterior Signage
projects.summary: Four-foot pickleballs mounted on a building façade, specified down to the rotation of each ball.
projects.description: Oversized pickleballs mounted on the outside of the club's building. The shop drawings fix the size, print specification, hardware and mounting method, and the rotation of each ball so they read as three balls in motion.
projects.brief: Turn a playful idea into signage that can be fabricated, mounted on an existing façade and installed consistently.
process: Placed the balls on a photo of the building with measurements to check scale and position.
Specified 3 mm white metal composite faceplates with a direct yellow print and matte laminate.
Called out aluminum angle hardware and mechanical plus epoxy mounting, with each ball rotated 0°, 30° and 60° from top to bottom.

projects.title: 30000 Feet — Rain Garden Sign
projects.summary: An interpretive sign that explains how rain gardens keep pollution out of the Mississippi River.
projects.description: A post-mounted interpretive sign for a rain garden at 30000 Feet. The artwork explains the science in a diagram; the shop drawing covers the panel, mounting plate, post and the 45-degree angle that makes it readable for a standing visitor.
projects.brief: Help visitors understand what a rain garden does, using a sign that is clear at a glance and durable outdoors.
process: Designed the sign artwork around a cross-section diagram of the garden.
Drew the panel, mounting plate and side view next to a human figure to check height and angle.
Specified a UV-printed metal composite panel on a galvanized steel post.

projects.title: Prior Lake Polar Plunge — Banner
projects.summary: A 30-foot event banner built to be read from the road, with a removable date.
projects.description: A winter event banner for the Prior Lake Polar Plunge. The icy lettering and bold type read at a distance, and the date is a separate vinyl piece so the same banner can be used in future years.
projects.brief: Promote the event to people passing by, and make the banner reusable year after year.
process: Designed the banner at 360 × 36 inches.
Specified double-sided printed mesh with a sewn hem and grommets every 24 inches.
Drew the date as a removable vinyl element so only that piece needs replacing.

projects.title: ADA Slider Sign — Animated Render
projects.summary: An exploded 3D view of a sliding room-sign assembly.
projects.description: A render of a sliding ADA sign: the backplate, the sliding panels and the inserts shown apart. The short animation shows how the parts come together.
projects.brief: Show how the sign is built in a way that is easy to understand without reading a drawing.
process: Modeled each part of the assembly.

projects.title: Fast Tempo — Illustrated Book
projects.summary: A bold, purple, music-driven children's book with a character-led layout.
projects.description: Illustration and layout for Fast Tempo. Saturated color, hand-lettered titles and a cast of characters keep the pages moving at the pace the title promises.
projects.brief: Make the pages feel like music: energetic, colorful and easy for young readers to follow.
process: Developed the characters and a limited, high-contrast palette.
Laid out the spreads with large hand-lettered type.
Mocked up the finished book as a printed object.

projects.title: Spots and Dots — Illustrated Book
projects.summary: A two-color blue book of dogs, spots and playful type.
projects.description: A children's book built on one blue and white palette. Simple line illustration and chunky lettering carry the story with very little else on the page.
projects.brief: Tell a simple story with a restrained palette and big, readable type.
process: Limited the palette to one blue and white.
Drew the characters in clean line work.
Set playful lettering into the scenes and mocked up the printed book.
